newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: All Colombia military ordered back to barracks.
newsitem.headline: All Colombia military ordered back to barracks.

text.p: All Colombian army and police leave was cancelled on Wednesday and all military personnel were ordered back to barracks amid threat of a new offensive by leftist rebels, the defence ministry said.

"Unfortunately the (poor) law and order situation in Colombia is a reality that nobody can deny and the armed forces are working to defend the interests of all citizens," Defence Minister Gilberto Echeverri said in a press statement.

The decision was prompted by a series of attacks that began with clashes between Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels in southern Caqueta province attacks last Sunday, in which five soldiers died and 17 others were injured.
Three policemen were killed and two others were injured in northern Bolivar province overnight on Monday when an estimated 300 National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels raided a police post.

And in the early hours on Wednesday, ELN insurgents blocked the main highway from Bogota to the northwest city of Medellin, burning at least 11 tractor-trailers and killing one motorist who tried to avoid the rebel roadblock.
"The provinces that need the greatest police presence are (northwest) Antioquia, (northern) Cesar, (northeast) Santander and Caqueta," national police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano said.

Earlier on Wednesday army chief Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett told reporters that the army did not have sufficient helicopters to reinforce army or police units that came under rebel attack in remote areas.
